newsitem.title: USA: Texas lottery executive director dismissed.
newsitem.headline: Texas lottery executive director dismissed.

text.p: The executive director of the Texas Lottery Commission was dismissed on Tuesday after disclosures about a close friend's work for GTECH Holdings Corp, which operates the state's lottery.

Texas Lottery Commission Executive Director Nora Linares first came under fire in November after it was disclosed that Mike Moeller had been paid $30,000 in 1991-92 by GTECH but had performed no work under the contract. Linares has described Moeller as a close friend.

Moeller, a former Texas assistant agriculture commissioner, received paychecks from GTECH at the New Mexico home of a cousin of Linares. He is now serving time in a federal prison on an unrelated corruption charge.
"I know they acted in the best interests of the lottery and the people of Texas," Gov. George Bush said, referring to the unanimous decision by the lottery commissioners to dismiss Linares.
Linares declined comment after the commission meeting adjourned.

A federal grand jury in Austin, Texas, is investigating operations of the state's lottery. The Texas Rangers, the state's police force, were called in to secure lottery files after documents were discovered missing at commission offices late last year.

John Hill, a former Democratic Texas attorney general and chief justice appointed to the commission last week, said the executive director's dismissal had been prompted by the controversy and a lawsuit filed by Linares against the lottery.
Linares sued the lottery commission for allegedly undermining her authority with disclosures of her relationship with Moeller and reports of his GTECH contract.
The sentencing of a former GTECH official in New Jersey later this month could shed more light on the Rhode Island-based company's operations in Texas, officials said.
Former GTECH national sales manager J. David Smith, who hired Moeller in Texas, faces sentencing in Newark, N.J., for taking kickbacks from political consultants hired by GTECH in New Jersey.
